title: Execute the half-sum CLEAR on fixed tapes with a complete scan bill
body:
This gives a fixed-tape execution and complete local scan bill for the exact half-sum CLEAR circuit in [PR #7721](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7721). At width 1076, the emitted program uses **589,841 unit data instructions and 11,206,982 interpreter steps**. It preserves all donors, implements the target XOR and invalid flag, restores every work cell and temporary bit, and returns all 26 heads. **No new kappa is claimed.**

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/PROOF.md), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/RESULT.json), [emitted binary program](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/PROGRAM-1076.bits.gz), [compiler and tape executor](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/tape.py), [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credit](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/CREDITS.md). The [scoped claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19715135) answers the source's released tape-layout question.

The machine has 25 data tapes, one read-only program tape, a five-symbol alphabet, two temporary control bits and a width-independent finite decoder. Nine binary bits encode each unit movement, control read, target toggle or cell initialization/retirement. The program is read and returned in full. No random-access gate lookup is assumed during execution.

| Resource at width 1076 | Exact count |
| --- | ---: |
| Data bit cells | 24,788 |
| Work bit cells, included above | 15,103 |
| Peak data markers | 50 |
| Marked program cells | 5,308,571 |
| Unit data instructions | 589,841 |
| Interpreter steps | 11,206,982 |

For every positive width, the proof gives `L<=1222w+2952` instructions and `19L+3<=23218w+56091` interpreter steps. It charges ripple access, flags, output copy, reverse execution, initialization, retirement and all head returns. This bound follows from the literal column loops; it is not fitted to measured values. Work cells start blank and return blank. The original external markers and program remain unchanged.

The entrance supplies the marked width-dependent program, input blocks, origins and reserved blank regions. **Uniform physical program generation/loading and enclosing stock/reset services remain open.** This is a classical multi-tape execution model; transition-level reversible control is not claimed. The complete external XOR map is reversible and its local workspace is restored. No selected owned-erasure or precision-tape assumption is discharged.

Base: `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. The six scientific files from PR #7721, published head `8f6279527c4362e2638737c90fa18c3cfec724fa`, are retained unchanged. Its [source proof and credit](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/8f6279527c4362e2638737c90fa18c3cfec724fa/research/half-sum-clear-circuit/README.md) establish the all-width arithmetic map. Its source verifier is rerun. The native event88937 identification is inherited from [PR #7687](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7687) and its [exact interface](https://github.com/SYLforge/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e5ba67dfd6237a1a3acf4d67098d3242adee8229/research/clean-rational-clear-witness/README.md); that whole native check was not rerun. [PR #3233](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3233) prices a different pooled field ADD; no code or constant is reused from it.

Run with CPython 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/half-sum-clear-tape
```

Each registered command prints the retained source result, then:

```text
PASS_HALF_SUM_CLEAR_FIXED_TAPE {'1': 1024, '2': 65536, '1076': 32} 11206982
```

Normal and optimized replay pass. The tape checker executes all 1,024 width-one combinations, all 65,536 width-two donor tuples with varied output bits, and the 32 published width-1076 fixtures. It checks every tape cell and head against direct integer arithmetic. Five damaged streams are rejected. An endpoint-preserving extra right/left detour costs exactly 38 additional steps. Source bytes, committed history/modes, package export, sealed read-only Git-free replay, public links and rendered publication readback pass. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44372462678/job/135042649052) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

No full caller or outer calculation changes: the selected saving remains `.00363005817` with all five framework assumptions. Program preparation, global stock/reset, rounded producer reachability and native/caller admission remain explicit obligations. Full predecessor suites, selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were not run. This is source-aware author checking, not blind, independent human or formal acceptance. No selected-frontier or other workstream change is included.

Credit Nick Petalas for the specialized circuit, proof and verifier; SYLforge for the source word, coordinate identification, validity interface and comparator; and the retained native/compiler contributors. The source README verifies these attributions. Original files and notices remain. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0.
